id: Cat Power. The Greatest. On Tour.-The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Cat Power. The Greatest. On Tour.
venue: The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington
long_description:
Twenty years on, The Greatest still sounds like midnight.

This summer, Cat Power returns to New Zealand for a run of special shows performing her seminal 2006 album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular catalogues in contemporary music.

Recorded in Memphis with members of the legendary Hi Rhythm section, The Greatest remains a defining statement from Marshall: smoky, soulful and heartbreakingly intimate. Featuring enduring tracks including “The Greatest”, “Living Proof” and “Lived in Bars”, the album cemented Cat Power as one of the most influential voices of her generation.

To mark the album’s 20th anniversary, these rare performances will revisit the record front to back, a chance to experience its quiet power, emotional depth and timeless beauty in the live setting it deserves.

Support for these shows will be Lawrence Arabia - the acclaimed musical project of Christchurch-born singer-songwriter James Milne, one of New Zealand’s most celebrated and influential contemporary artists. Across a career spanning nearly two decades, Milne has released a string of critically acclaimed albums, earning an APRA Silver Scroll for his song Apple Pie Bed, the inaugural Taite Music Prize, and multiple Aotearoa Music Awards.

There are few artists who can hold a room the way Cat Power can. Experience the magic of The Greatest and re-enter the orbit of the early millennium in these raw, hypnotic shows in November.

name: DECEITS Aotearoa Tour
venue: Valhalla, 154 Vivian Street, Wellington
long_description: Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

long_description:
Few DJs understand a dancefloor quite like Marcellus Pittman. A cornerstone of contemporary Detroit dance music, Pittman brings decades of experience, deep musical knowledge and an unmistakable sense of groove to Meow Nui on Friday 27 November.

A true master behind the decks, Pittman is known for sets that move effortlessly between rolling, low-slung house, high-tempo disco, raw techno, funk, post-punk and deeper late-night selections. His approach is instinctive and unpredictable, built around meticulous mixing and an ability to read a room and take it exactly where it needs to go.
Pittman first came to prominence alongside Theo Parrish on Essential Selections Volume 1 before becoming one quarter of the legendary Three Chairs, alongside Parrish, Kenny Dixon Jr. (Moodymann) and Rick Wilhite. He later founded his own Unirhythm imprint and released music through labels including Omar-S’ FXHE, while also collaborating as part of the T.O.M. Project and Rotating Assembly.

His productions carry the same raw, spacious and deeply human quality as his DJ sets, pairing tough drum programming with subtle, unexpected detail. It is a sound rooted firmly in Detroit while remaining completely his own.

From intimate basements to major clubs and festivals across the world, Marcellus Pittman has built a reputation as one of dance music’s most respected selectors. This is a rare chance to experience a true Detroit heavyweight on the Meow Nui system.

Support from Benny Salvador, one of Aotearoa’s most exciting young selectors, blending house, techno, electro, disco-funk, dub, boogie and beyond.

Don’t miss your chance to be in the room.

long_description:
The Little Grimley Amateur Dramatic Society from Limelight Theatre returns in another hilarious comedy from David Tristram. With a membership of just four, the society has survived budget constraints, artistic disagreements, and countless theatrical disasters. This time, faced with the challenge of finding a suitable play, chairman Gordon decides there’s only one solution: an evening of Shakespeare.

After all, what could possibly go wrong when an amateur dramatic group takes on the world’s greatest playwright?

As Gordon’s ambitious vision collides with limited resources, Bernard’s enthusiastic improvisation, Joyce’s personal distractions, and Margaret’s diva tendencies, the production quickly descends into chaos. With tempers flaring, egos colliding, and Shakespeare being interpreted in ways he never intended, keeping the show on track becomes a performance in itself.

Packed with the witty dialogue, larger-than-life characters, and laugh-out-loud moments that have made the Little Grimley series a favourite with audiences, To Be Or Not To Bother is a delightful evening of pure comedy entertainment.

long_description:
Mini mosaics are really quick and simple to make - but can create a really popping design with beautiful coloured glass and fun shapes to decorate.

We will use gorgeous coloured glass pieces to create our designs on small flat backings - this is a very beginner-friendly method, and allows for several pieces to be made within the class time.

This class runs over two sessions; this means you have time to do all the parts of a mosaic. The planning, the glueing, and then your pieces have time to dry so you can then do the grouting and finishing off. A fantastic course that's super fun as a one-off experience - or to dip your toe into working with glass mosaics.

You can have the finished items as either:
A set ready to hang on a wall as singles
On a large sturdy jumpring ready to hang as a cute pendant set (or earrings).
On a cord for an heirloom Christmas ornament.

Preparing your bases and materials
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.

In the second session we will continue finishing off your mosaics, selecting the grout you like, and learning how to apply and clean up this essential part of a mosaic.

Finally we will look at what mounting options and special additions you might want to add to your piece that will complete the design.

You are welcome to continue creating more mosaics and can purchase additional materials to do so. Any that require grouting after the class is completed can either:
Be completed by our team (for a small fee)
Be grouted by you later, we can supply the grout and some sealant for you to take home.

This is a warm, friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to start working with hand-cut glass terraria.

venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
long_description:
Gain the confidence and skills to maintain your bicycle in good working order, and to diagnose and fix some mechanical problems. Get familiar with bike terms and tools and learn through practical experience.

Have you recently started riding a bike and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?

Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?

This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.

Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!

Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.

Bring your pushbike along on the day, If you have the following, please bring them as well: A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.

(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
Fix a flat tyre
Adjust your bike to fit your body
Oil and clean your chain
Identify and fix some common brake problems

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
venue: Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Coastlands Theatre, 34a Raumati Rd, Paraparaumu
long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)

Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

For accessibility seating information and wheelchair space bookings please email kiaora@teraukura.nz or call 04)9740535 during office hours.
Door sales are only available if the event doesn't sell out prior.

This collaboration will be presented in both Kāpiti and Wellington.

Duration: Approximately 2 hours including interval.
